name: Migne.app — Patrologia Latina & Graeca, open
license: Latin/Greek public domain; English CC BY-NC 4.0 (per /method page)
description: Open reader for the whole of Migne, searchable by citation (e.g. 'PL 139, 473A'), with new English translations including many first-ever ones.

name: Lapide.org — Cornelius a Lapide commentary translated
license: Site calls its English 'public domain'. The GitHub repo has no license file.
languages: Latin -> English, plus ~35 other languages (Spanish, French, Portuguese, Tagalog, Swahili, Chinese, etc.)
description: AI (Claude) translation of the whole Lapide commentary into English and many other languages, with search and EPUBs. Content is going through a quality-control pass, and you can report errors as GitHub issues.
texts: Cornelius a Lapide SJ's Great Commentary on Scripture, plus other Latin works (Adam of Dryburgh, Riccioli, Sixtus of Siena, Pererius). EPUB downloads.

name: Bonaventure — Opera Omnia in English
license: English translation CC BY-NC 4.0 (© 2026, per the site footer); Latin public domain
description: The first complete English Opera Omnia of St. Bonaventure, drafted with an LLM from the Quaracchi Latin and checked against the printed page using a documented procedure.
texts: Quaracchi critical edition. Vol. I-IV (the full Commentary on the Sentences) and Vol. V (Breviloquium, Itinerarium, Collationes in Hexaemeron, disputed questions, sermons) are complete. Vol. VI scriptural commentaries in progress; the aim is all 10 volumes.
ai_detail: yes: LLM-drafted, then checked by a written procedure

name: ScholaThomistica

name: Mind of the Church

ai_detail: yes: AI-assisted per the maintainer's X posts

ai_detail: yes: AI-assisted, checked against the source (site says so)

name: Historical Christian Faith (writings and commentary databases)

description: Open, searchable databases of early Christian writings and commentary verse by verse, kept on GitHub and built to be reused.
texts: Verse-by-verse patristic commentary database plus a writings database. Some new public-domain AI translations, e.g. Bede on Acts. Second repo: HistoricalChristianFaith/Writings-Database.

name: @ViaEximii: Baroque Thomist and controversialist translations (Internet Archive)
license: Some items marked Public Domain Mark 1.0 (e.g. the De Anima and Billuart predetermination items); most have no license set
description: The most prolific individual translator of Baroque scholastics and Counter-Reformation controversialists on X. Uploads are free on the Internet Archive's opensource collection; several say they are AI-assisted (Claude).
texts: About 18 Internet Archive uploads (2024-2026) by the same translator: John of St. Thomas (Cursus Philosophicus: Logic, De Anima, Generation & Corruption; Defense of the Trinity; Essence/Existence/Subsistence), Gonet (Manuale Thomistarum vols. I-IV, Physical Premotion, Efficacy of the Divine Will), Billuart (Middle Knowledge, Divine Predetermination), Melchior Cano (De Locis Theologicis), Cornaeus (Ens Rationis Luthero-Calvinicum, 2026-07-27), Erbermann (Bellarmine Vindicated, 2026-08-09). Related uploads I could not attribute: Elorduy on Suárez's beatification (2026-08-18), Billuart Sermons ('translated with Sonnet 5'), Billuart on the Trinity, Clypeus Theologiae Thomisticae.
ai_detail: yes for several items (descriptions say 'AI translation'; translator credits Claude)

texts: PL works with Latin-Japanese parallel text, starting with Tertullian (PL 1). The site reports 409 works and 126,522 sections, citable by Migne column.
ai_detail: yes: Claude translation plus LLM review, no human expert check (site says so)
